core.title: Build route.sequence as ordered {layer}.{action} steps
core.when: The planner writes or changes route.sequence.
core.then: Write route.sequence as ordered {layer}.{action} transitions from the route_step vocabulary, flowing through the layer roles in the profile's dependency order (profile: roles.layers) as needed (include only the layers the scenario uses; a route triggered from an external integration may start at integration, as in the event flow).
prefer: Event (starts at integration): integration.call_external -> application.aggregate -> domain.mutate -> integration.persist.
avoid: Free-form step names or layers outside the profile's layer roles (profile: roles.layers).

Listing steps unordered or in an order that does not reflect the actual sequence of transitions; do not reject or reorder an integration-initiated route like the event flow just because it begins at integration.
Padding the route with layers the scenario does not need.
core.why: A fixed {layer}.{action} vocabulary makes the layer flow behind each acceptance explicit and mechanically checkable.
evidence: Every route.sequence entry matches {layer}.{action} and is in the allowed route_step vocabulary.

Steps are ordered as the scenario's transitions occur, consistent with the canonical shapes: command and query flows run presentation -> application -> (domain) -> integration; the event flow starts at integration.call_external and then proceeds application -> domain -> integration.
verification: Check that each route.sequence entry is one route_step term (a single {layer}.{action} transition in a route sequence) drawn from the allowed route_step vocabulary: presentation.{command,query,display}, application.{use_case,query,aggregate}, domain.{create,validate,mutate,policy}, integration.{read,persist,call_external}, with the layer names taken from the profile's layer roles.

Check step order against the canonical examples, all of which must pass: presentation_flow [presentation.command, application.use_case, domain.validate, integration.persist]; query_flow [presentation.query, application.query, integration.read]; event_flow [integration.call_external, application.aggregate, domain.mutate, integration.persist].

Order is not a strict monotonic layer check: layers may be skipped (query_flow omits domain) and an integration step may both open and close a route (event_flow); the check must not reject or reorder an integration-initiated route just because it begins at integration. All three canonical examples must pass any order check.

fires: Planner authors a new acceptance that includes a route.sequence.
Planner edits the steps or order of an existing acceptance's route.sequence.
doesNotFire: Editing only the acceptance's prose or Given/When/Then text without touching route.sequence.
Coder changes production code with no acceptance artifact change.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's layer roles in dependency order. The core draws the allowed layer names (avoid: no layers outside them) and the direction of the route flow in the then-clause from this ordered list.

neutralityNotes: This convention is method-level: every agent-facing item of bun.json names only method roles (planner), layer roles (presentation/application/domain/integration), and task-model fields (route.sequence), so no item is bunOnly and no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, suffix or path appears in the core. The only stack-parameterized data is the layer set and its flow order, sourced from roles.layers; with the Bun value (presentation, application, domain, integration) the core imposes exactly the Bun obligation. bun.json declares no exceptions, so core.unless is the empty array, matching the schema. The route_step action vocabulary per layer is treated as rule (method) data and stays in the core, since it comes from the method's term definition rather than from the stack; a stack wanting different step actions would need a proposed vocabulary key, which was not required here. The change fact (route.sequence added or modified) still needs a structural-diff observer (needs_new_observer); the over-approximation via file_kind+operation until then is preserved. The activation facts' explanatory notes were dropped because the neutral fact schema carries only fact/values/observability; their content is restated in the classification notes and is not part of the obligation.
